label: HUMAN?
text:
Something I got wrong for years:

I thought code review was about finding bugs.

It isn't. It's about spreading context.

The bugs you catch in review are the cheap ones. The expensive ones need tests.

But the knowledge transfer? That only happens in review.

Changed how I review entirely.

text: Proud to share that our team just shipped the new payments dashboard after 8 months of work. Huge credit to the four engineers who carried this. It now handles 40k merchants and cut support tickets by about 30%. Genuinely the hardest thing I've worked on.

label: SLOP?
text: Most engineering managers optimise for velocity. The good ones optimise for the half-life of a decision. If a choice takes two weeks to make and six months to reverse, you've mispriced the meeting. I've been thinking about this since a conversation with a colleague last month and haven't fully worked it out yet.
